samples: This is a small, pure library (no I/O or permissions needed) for handling semantic version numbers of the form major.minor.patch, without pre-release or build suffixes. It parses text into a version, reporting whether the failure was a wrong number of parts or a non-numeric or negative part, prints versions back as dotted text, and compares them by major, then minor, then patch. It also offers a compatibility check (same major version and not older than the required one) and a function that picks the greatest version from a list, returning nothing if the list is empty.

This module handles semantic version numbers of the form major.minor.patch (such as 1.4.2): it parses text into a version, prints it back the same way, and compares versions by major, then minor, then patch. Parsing is strict, accepting only exactly three non-negative whole-number parts and returning a specific error for the wrong number of parts or a non-numeric part. It also offers a compatibility check (same major version and not older than required) and a way to find the newest version in a list, though it does not support pre-release or build suffixes.

This module handles semantic version numbers of the form major.minor.patch (such as 1.4.2): it turns text into a version, prints it back as text, and orders versions by major, then minor, then patch. Parsing reports a clear error if the text doesn't have exactly three parts or if a part isn't a non-negative whole number. It also offers a compatibility check (same major version and not older than the required one) and a way to pick the greatest version from a list, but it doesn't support pre-release or build suffixes like "-beta" or "+build".

This module handles semantic version numbers of the form major.minor.patch: it parses text into a version (reporting a clear error if the text doesn't have exactly three parts or a part isn't a non-negative whole number), prints versions back as dotted text, and compares them by major, then minor, then patch. It also offers a compatibility check (a candidate satisfies a requirement if it has the same major version and is not older) and a way to pick the greatest version from a list, returning nothing if the list is empty. It is pure, needs no permissions, and does not support pre-release or build suffixes, so it suits plain numeric versions only.

This module handles simple semantic version numbers (major.minor.patch, such as 1.4.2): it parses text into a version, prints it back as dotted text, and orders versions by major, then minor, then patch. Parsing fails with a clear error if the text doesn't have exactly three parts or if a part isn't a non-negative whole number, and it trims surrounding whitespace first. It also offers a compatibility check (same major version and not older than the required one) and a function that picks the greatest version from a list, returning nothing for an empty list; it does not support pre-release or build suffixes like "-beta" or "+build".
